🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin holds the mid-$80Ks after a historic Q3 and a week of ETF inflows, while fallout from the $387.5M Bitget hack reignites the debate over decentralization and responsibility. 🛡️ THORChain Rejects Bitget's Plea to Block Hacker Addresses Bitget CEO Gracy Chen formally asked THORChain to refuse service to wallets tied to the exchange's $387.5M breach after attackers used the protocol to swap stolen ETH and BNB into native Bitcoin. THORChain declined, citing its permissionless design. Meanwhile, the hacker has moved about $83M in XRP that Ripple has no way to freeze. Bitget says customer balances are covered and withdrawals resume in stages from Sept. 28. Read full story ₿ Bitcoin Heads for Its Second-Best Q3 Ever as Ether Sets a Record Bitcoin has gained roughly 43.5% this quarter, climbing from about $58,500 to around $84,000 — a Q3 bested only by 2017. Ether did even better, rising about 71% for its strongest third quarter on record, supported by stronger ETF demand, rising spot volume and restrained profit-taking. More details 📈 Bitcoin ETFs Stretch Inflow Streak to Seven Days and $2.98B U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs added $134.5M on Friday, their seventh straight day of inflows, pulling in close to $3B since Sept. 17. The run marks a sharp reversal from mid-September outflows and has flipped 2026 ETF flows back into positive territory. Read more 📜 Michael Saylor Proposes a "Bill of Digital Rights" Strategy's executive chairman published an essay arguing the AI era needs digital-asset freedoms rather than restrictions: the rights to create, issue, custody, transfer and use digital assets. He also called for banks to hold and lend against Bitcoin on normal commercial terms, criticizing heavy Basel capital charges.
